summary.verdict: unviable — value per customer below the acquisition floor

claude_analysis.tam_assessment: Niche market: buyers are EEG research labs, BCI hobbyists (e.g. OpenBCI users on r/BCI) and clinical neurophysiology units, and there is no Google Trends or Hacker News signal.
claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: Willingness to pay is very low: the observed anchors are $1-2 one-time, and free converters already cover this (convert.guru, MNE, EEGLAB, open-source GitHub tools), so even ~$10/yr is optimistic.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The only restriction found ('licensed attorney') comes from an article about legal consulting and doesn't apply to EEG data conversion, and no government sources came up.
key_risks: Free open-source tools (MNE-Python, EEGLAB, BESA, EDF2EEG converters) already handle format conversion
Value per customer (~$2) is far below the $200 acquisition floor
Vendor and documentation sites own the search results, so paid acquisition may be the only channel
key_opportunities: The EEG format landscape is fragmented (EDF, BDF, NeuroScan, WinEEG, BrainVision), so conversion is a real recurring need
The consumer BCI community (OpenBCI) is growing, and some users don't want to install Python toolchains
claude_analysis.value_reasoning: 10,000 potential customers × $10/yr ≈ $100,000 total addressable annual revenue.
claude_analysis.probability_reasoning: The below-acquisition-floor ceiling applies (2 price observations), so the cap is 0.01, and with a crowded field of free incumbents realistic penetration is under 1%.
